text: The GECKO method extends genome-scale metabolic models by:
choices: Incorporating enzyme kcat values and a constraint on total enzyme usage (proteome allocation)
Adding Boolean gene-regulatory rules that switch reactions on or off over time (rFBA)
Coupling flux balance analysis to dynamic equations for extracellular metabolites over time (dynamic FBA)
Combining multiple organism-specific models into a shared community model (SteadyCom/micom)
explanation: GECKO reformulates each reaction in enzyme-catalyzed form using kcat values and adds a constraint on total enzyme usage, capturing proteome allocation and predicting enzyme saturation. Boolean regulatory switching is rFBA's contribution, coupling FBA to time-varying extracellular metabolite dynamics is dynamic FBA (dFBA), and stacking multiple organisms' GEMs with a shared compartment describes community modeling approaches like SteadyCom or micom, all distinct extensions from GECKO.
